A1.justification: Both PDFs describe Diff-PIC and provide readable text, equations, figures and tables. V1 includes appendices S1–S6; v3 ends after the references, retaining selected implementation details in Section 4.1. The supplied material supports reliable comparison.

before.justification: Section 4 and Appendix S2 report original interpolation, extrapolation, energy, runtime and ablation results using OSIRIS-generated electric fields.

after.justification: Section 4 reports original electric-field generation results, comparisons with GAN-PIC and NF-PIC, energy evaluations and computational efficiency measurements.

M1.justification: The conditional U-Net, positional and polynomial encodings, MLP refinement, and rectified-flow/reflow procedure remain unchanged. PICE becomes PIPE, and the output description explicitly focuses on electric fields; these clarify the existing method rather than establish an algorithmic change.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same described 6,615-simulation OSIRIS corpus and E1/E2 electric-field tasks conditioned on temperatures and laser intensity. Extrapolation coverage contracts from 10%, 20%, 40% and 80% beyond training ranges to only 10% and 20%, removing the more extreme input conditions.

E2.justification: V1's main comparisons use B-1, with an MLP replacing the proposed encoder, and B-2, using 1,000-step DDPM sampling. V3 replaces these with PIPE-equipped GAN-PIC and NF-PIC in accuracy and efficiency comparisons. The appendix comparisons involving convolutional encoding, unrefined embeddings, DDIM and ODE-only acceleration also disappear.

E3.justification: The reported interpolation sample count changes from 700 simulations to 500, retaining the 80/20 split. Tables replace SWD and MMD with electric-field MAE and RMSE, evaluated on normalized data, while retaining FID. Energy-error evaluation remains. These are substantive reported protocol changes; the PDFs do not establish which experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: V3 removes Appendix S2 and Table S1's encoder, acceleration and 200–1,000-sample sensitivity studies. It also drops the 40% and 80% extrapolation tests. The field visualizations and temporal energy checks remain, but the controlled evidence isolating the two proposed components is lost.

E5.justification: V1 Table S1 reports FID and SWD with uncertainty values, such as FID 1.62 ± 0.05. V3 removes this limited uncertainty reporting and presents point estimates only. Neither version specifies the meaning of these intervals or provides repeated-run counts or seeds.

E6.justification: V3 adds GAN-PIC/NF-PIC results and electric-field error measurements while removing internal-baseline, SWD/MMD and ablation entries. Diff-PIC's E1 10% extrapolation FID changes from 3.87 to 1.74 under the revised sampling protocol, so this is not an established same-setting improvement. Its interpolation FIDs, displayed energy errors and 16,200-fold GPU speedup remain unchanged.

T1.justification: Section 4.3 revises the stated PIC complexity argument from pairwise N^2 scaling to T N log N, explicitly including time steps. The polynomial encoding and rectified-flow objective remain mathematically equivalent. Neither version supplies a formal proof of the proposed method's guarantees.

C1.justification: The central contributions—diffusion-based PIC substitution, continuous parameter encoding and one-step acceleration—remain. V3 adds headline claims of average MAE/RMSE/FID reductions against GAN-PIC and NF-PIC and extends the introductory speedup claim to generative alternatives. The 16,200-fold comparison with traditional PIC is retained.

C2.justification: V3 adds an energy-landscape/Langevin analogy and a polarization-based rationale for representing electric fields in two dimensions. It removes the appendix interpretations concerning encoder benefits, acceleration's fidelity–speed tradeoff and saturation around 700 samples, together with the limitation concerning poorly represented corner cases. This substantially changes the explanatory and qualification content.

D1.justification: The U-Net configuration, 600 epochs, batch size 64, learning rate, embedding size and polynomial order move from Appendix S1 into Section 4.1. V3 adds normalization and baseline-adaptation details but omits explicit separate encoder training, single-layer MLP dimensionality preservation, PyTorch identification and OSIRIS licensing. Neither PDF establishes an actual public resource release.

R1.justification: V3 adds references supporting energy-based modeling, GAN/StyleGAN, diffusion normalizing flow and additional PIC implementations, while removing several background citations. Section 5's discussion of earlier PIC acceleration and scientific diffusion applications, and the claimed novelty of a diffusion surrogate for LPI, remain largely unchanged.

P1.justification: The abstract, introduction, diffusion background and distillation explanation are substantially rewritten. Condition terminology becomes parameter terminology throughout, implementation material moves into the main evaluation section, and the six-section appendix disappears. These changes substantially reshape the exposition despite retaining the main section sequence.

P2.justification: Figure 1's fusion illustration becomes a cost–fidelity comparison diagram. Figure 2 is redrawn, with its encoder detail presented separately as Figure 3. Extrapolation tables are merged and restructured, and Table S1 disappears. The existing field and energy visualizations are retained with new numbering and placement.

improvement.justification: GAN/NF comparisons, field-error metrics and clearer exposition are useful additions. However, removing all component and sample-size ablations, their uncertainty reporting and the corner-case limitation weakens support for the retained contributions. V3 also claims orders-of-magnitude speedups over generative alternatives, although Table 3 implies only about 1.04-fold over GAN-PIC and 17.6-fold over NF-PIC on GPU. These evidential and qualification losses outweigh the gains, producing a limited net decline.
